reasoning_traces.think:
The system operates through three sequential stages: simulation, curation, and contest-specific optimization. In Stage 1, GSE generates player projections from post-game simulations, which are then filtered through a 10-gate accuracy protocol (G1–G5) to eliminate suboptimal candidates. This curated pool forms the basis for Stage 2, where dedicated DFS simulations (10,000 worlds) compute performance distributions. The third stage uses MILP solvers to construct optimized lineups under salary and overlap constraints. Each primitive is grounded in mathematical optimization principles—set theory for curation, stochastic simulation for contest modeling, and integer programming for lineup construction. Failure modes include overfitting to historical data, insufficient simulation coverage, or constraint violations that reduce lineup diversity. Dualities emerge between projection accuracy and lineup robustness, where higher variance in projections necessitates more conservative lineup strategies.
